primary_sources.title: FP Markets FAQ, server time
primary_sources.support: Broker uses GMT+2/GMT+3 so daily candles follow the New York close. Current webpage alone is not a date-by-date historical source certificate.

primary_sources.title: FP Markets Metatrader Product Disclosure Statement, 29 March 2021, section 5.4, printed page 47
primary_sources.support: Defines New York-local 17:00 as server 00:00 for financing. This historical primary source supports the nominal New-York-close server convention.

primary_sources.title: Nasdaq Systems hours of operation
primary_sources.support: Primary exchange source lists the regular session as 09:30 through 16:00 Eastern. Used only to flag unusual raw ETF session labels, not to certify broker CFD quotes.

nominal_clock_inference.formula: Interpret broker wall datetime minus seven hours in America/New_York, then convert to UTC. The seven hours are a wall-clock difference, not a fixed UTC offset.
nominal_clock_inference.basis: Broker 00:00 equals New York-local 17:00 in both historical PDS and current FAQ.
nominal_clock_inference.calendar_2024_2025: 40 weekdays, 20 each year, differ from Europe/Helsinki by one hour.
nominal_clock_inference.source_exception_handling: No favorable clock selection, arbitrary timestamp shift, data deletion or correction rerun occurred. Resolve anomalous sources independently before any exact external-session binding economics.

source_lines: 391-406 external-local schedule converted to UTC and directly matched to raw index
family_findings.meaning: All 965 original complete events are reproducible from timestamps. Under the broker nominal convention they sample 2 or 3 hours before the declared open. The known adverse numbers describe that shifted implementation, not a valid falsification of London 08:00 / New York 09:30. Raw-history exceptions mean the nominal offsets are not individually certified physical instants.

source_lines: 359-405 external and target raw time indexes
437-446 New York schedule to UTC epoch
family_findings.meaning: AUDCHF and target series share raw broker encoding, so their relative ordering may remain causal, but the declared New York 10:00..15:30 slots map nominally to 08:00..13:30 in winter and 07:00..12:30 in summer. The original adverse result does not falsify the correctly aligned declared slot hypothesis.

source_lines: 31-33 Helsinki server zone and New York 15:30
family_findings.meaning: Helsinki matches nominal broker winter/summer offsets except US/EU transition gaps. On 40 development weekdays the nominal lookup samples New York 14:30 instead of 15:30. Rolling historical signal/risk references can propagate this beyond those dates; economic impact is not bounded to 40 rows. Additionally QQQ/TQQQ raw 2025-03-10..14 sessions are 17:30..23:59 rather than predominant 16:30..22:59, so a formula replacement alone is not certified source repair. Original output is descriptive for the implemented mixed-time sample; exact intended-session adverse authority is suspended.

The strategy uses observed H4 bar indices for features, holds and exits, a common monotone map for cross-symbol ordering, and raw server time for swaps. Across all seven 2024-2025 source series the corrected nominal map changes no UTC date/year or declared year-boundary membership; raw index order is unchanged. This specific clock defect corrects event UTC labels but does not invalidate its existing adverse development economic conclusion. No economic rerun or broader source-quality certification was performed.

The original 514 complete development event dates reproduce from raw timestamps. Of those, 38 fall in US/EU DST mismatch windows and the nominal London event shifts an hour early. Rolling references can affect later dates; no profit effect is inferred. The complete intended-fix hypothesis was not validly adjudicated, though original mixed-time outputs and its closure remain immutable.
